page.title: Creative Agency vs Production Company for Associations
page.description: Compare scope, timeline, pricing, and handoff quality to choose the right partner for association events and campaigns.
page.h1: How do you decide on creative agency vs production company for associations?
page.definition: Creative agency vs production company for associations is a procurement decision that matches event scope, brand strategy, and internal capacity to the right external partner type. Creative agencies lead brand strategy and multi-channel campaigns. Production companies lead live execution and technical delivery. The choice depends on whether the association needs concept development or show operations.
page.quick_answer: Map your event goals to scope: choose a creative agency for brand strategy and multi-channel campaigns, choose a production company for live execution and technical delivery, or hire both when strategy and execution need separate owners.

sections.h2: What does a creative agency deliver that a production company does not?

blocks.p: Creative agencies own brand strategy, messaging frameworks, and multi-channel campaign design for associations. They develop creative concepts, write copy, design visual systems, and plan distribution across email, social, web, and print. They typically do not run live shows, manage encoders, or operate streaming platforms.

ul: Brand positioning and voice guidelines
Campaign themes and creative concepts
Copywriting for landing pages, emails, and social
Design systems for slides, graphics, and video assets
Content calendars and distribution plans

sections.h2: What does a production company deliver that a creative agency does not?

blocks.p: Production companies own live execution, technical crew, and stream reliability for virtual and hybrid events. They provide show callers, camera operators, audio engineers, platform operators, and backup streams. They follow a run of show, rehearse speakers, and deliver edited recordings. They typically do not create brand strategy or campaign assets.

ul: Run of show and cue sheets
Speaker rehearsals and technical checks
Live switching, lower thirds, and graphics playback
Backup stream and encoder redundancy
Edited recording and highlight clips delivered post-event

sections.h2: How do scope and timeline differ between the two?

blocks.p: Creative agency engagements span months for strategy and asset libraries; production company engagements compress to weeks for a single event.

ul: Creative agency: discovery, strategy, concept rounds, asset production, approval cycles — typically eight to twelve weeks for a full campaign
Production company: intake, brief, run of show build, rehearsals, live day, post-production — typically three to four weeks for a webinar, six to eight weeks for a summit
Overlap window: creative assets must be finalized before production rehearsals begin
Internal approval gates often add one to two weeks on the creative side

sections.h2: What pricing models apply to each partner type?

blocks.p: Creative agencies bill retainers or project fees for strategy and assets; production companies bill per event or per day for crew and gear.

sections.h2: How do you evaluate handoff quality and ownership?

blocks.p: Clear handoffs require a shared brief, named owners, and approved deliverables before the event goes live.

ul: Single source brief document signed by both partners
Named creative lead and named production lead with contact escalation path
Asset delivery checklist: file formats, naming conventions, version numbers
Run of show review meeting with both teams present
Approval gate: creative signs off on branded assets; production signs off on technical readiness
Post-event debrief template captured within forty-eight hours

sections.h2: When should an association hire both a creative agency and a production company?

blocks.p: Hire both when brand strategy and live execution run on separate timelines or require different approval chains. West Peek Productions produces virtual, hybrid and webinar events and sets up marketing, content and creative operations. This split works when the association has an established brand system but needs specialist crew for a summit, or when a rebrand campaign must launch before the annual conference production begins.

faq.q: Can a creative agency also handle live production?
faq.a: Some large agencies have in-house production units, but most subcontract the technical crew. Verify who owns the run of show, the backup stream, and the encoder before assuming the agency covers both.

faq.q: What happens if the creative assets arrive late for rehearsal?
faq.a: Late assets force production to use placeholders, increasing rehearsal time and risk of on-air errors. Build a buffer of at least five business days between creative final approval and the first technical rehearsal.

faq.q: How do we split the budget between strategy and execution?
faq.a: Allocate roughly sixty percent to creative strategy and asset creation for a new campaign, forty percent to production for a single event. For recurring events with existing assets, shift to twenty percent creative refresh and eighty percent production.

faq.q: Who owns the post-event recording and clips?
faq.a: Ownership should be defined in the master services agreement. Typically the association owns the raw recording; the production company owns the edited deliverables unless the contract assigns all rights to the association.
